title: Tiny-batch p99 spike — investigation & TODOs
content:
Context:
- Noticed p99 jumps on production pool A starting 2026-03-10 03:00 UTC. Spike correlates with increased fraction of tiny batches (1-2 requests) after client-side change to aggressive flush.
- p50/p95 relatively stable; tail gets orders-of-magnitude worse intermittently.

Quick summary of observed numbers (prod sampling):
- tiny-batch (size=1-2): p50 ~35ms, p95 ~70ms, p99 ~420ms (outliers up to 1.2s)
- moderate-batch (8-16): p50 ~28ms, p95 ~40ms, p99 ~65ms
- traffic shift: tiny-batch fraction up from 12% -> 48% over last deploy window

Initial hypotheses (ranked):
1) KV cache (prefix cache) misses amplify prefill/first-token cost for tiny batches -> long-tail due to blocking I/O to cache or cold-hot memory movement.
2) Scheduling and context-switch jitter: when tiny batches arrive, worker is in a different execution path that triggers synchronous setup (alloc KV, warmup kernels) causing stalls.
3) CPU-GPU handoff/driver stalls for very small workloads are not amortized; kernel launch overhead dominated and shows non-linear variance with system load.
4) Networking/rpc layer: tiny requests are more sensitive to head-of-line queuing in our grpc threadpool (single-threaded path for small payloads).

Immediate repro plan (local + staging):
- Repro script to drive tiny batches to a single dedicated pod (use staging model replica).
  Commands to run:
  - ./tools/loadgen --endpoint http://staging-pool-A:8080/generate --concurrency 1 --batch-size 1 --qps 50 --duration 5m --trace-tokens
  - curl -v -H 'X-Test-Client: tiny-batcher' http://localhost:8080/v1/generate -d '{"model":"x-2b","input":"hello"}'
- Enable verbose tracing on single replica: env TRACE_LEVEL=debug TRACE_COMPONENTS=serving,kvcache,allocator
- Capture nvprof/nsys around spike window: docker exec -it runtime-worker nsys profile -o /tmp/spike.nsys --trace=cuda,osrt -- ./bin/worker --run-once
- Collect syscall /sched traces if repro shows long syscalls: sudo perf record -e sched:sched_switch -a sleep 60

Profiling notes so far (staging runs 2026-03-12):
- When tiny batch triggers, we see a synchronous path: allocate_temp_kv() -> populate_prefill() -> write-kv->sync-to-device. If KV cache returns miss, we do a CPU-side prefill which stalls generator thread ~300-700ms.
- nvprof shows frequent short kernel launches interleaved with memset/copy operations. Variance increases when GPU SM utilization is low.
- grpc threadpool trace: tiny-batch requests are handled by low-priority worker threads which occasionally get preempted by maintenance tasks (logflush, metrics ingest).

Quick ideas to alleviate (fast experiments):
- Favor pooled pre-allocated KV buffers for tiny-batch path to avoid malloc + cudaMemcpy on hot path. (Low-risk change, test unit + staging)
- Introduce an early async-prefetch: if request has known prefix signature, kick prefill on request receipt but don't block decode. Fall back to synchronous if prefill incomplete at decode start.
- Socket-level batching aggregation for same-client rapid-fire requests (proxy-level coalescing) — higher complexity, POC later.
- Adjust grpc-infer thread priorities or reserve core for tiny-batch handler to reduce preemption.

Concrete TODOs (owners + deadlines):
- Aria: implement pooled KV buffer prototype + unit tests. Target: 2026-03-15.
- Diego: add detailed perf counters for prefill vs decode time (histograms) and hook them into console route-level dashboard. Target: 2026-03-14.
- Mina: run loadgen P95/P99 sweep across batch sizes and collect nsys traces; upload artifacts to GH issue. Target: 2026-03-13 EOD.
- Ishaan: review grpc threadpool config and test priority tweak on staging; capture before/after traces. Target: 2026-03-14.

Open questions / things to validate:
- Are some client request patterns (same user, repeated small messages) causing cache churn? Look at affinity keys in logs (X-Client-ID).
- Is there OS-level interference on those replica machines at spike times? Check cron/backup windows and node-level metrics.
- What's the cost of introducing pooled buffers (memory pressure) for large model footprints? Need mem/alloc tradeoff analysis.

Notes to self (scratch):
- If pooled buffers help in staging, be careful with cleanup on model swap/rollout. Must tie to model-version lifecycle.
- Add metric: prefill_miss_ratio per-replica to the console, alert if > 5% and p99>200ms.
- Keep PRs small: start with instrumentation + non-invasive pool; rollback path via feature flag.

References / quick links to attach to tickets:
- GH PR with current prefill prototype: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4187
- Incident log (prod alert): ENG-9472
- Old notes on batching heuristics: /display/RUNTIME/Batching+Notes

Meeting sync: propose quick 30m runbook review Fri 2026-03-13 09:30 PT with Diego/Mina/Ishaan. Agenda: repro status, pooled-buffer tradeoffs, short-term mitigation (threadpool tweak).

End-of-day capture (2026-03-13):
- Confirmed repro in staging with similar p99 behavior (smaller magnitude).
- Prototype pooled-buffers reduced one class of 300ms stalls in isolated run; need sustained qps test.
- Next: instrument, run 6h soak, then try threadpool tweak if still present.

-- aria
